code: entries[num].offset = pos - start; entries[num].gen = gen; entries[num].type = xrefEntryUncompressed;
note: When constructXRef finds an object with num < size, resize() is not called, so entries[num].flags retains whatever value was in the previously allocated but uninitialized memory from greallocn in reserve().

greallocn_checkoverflow calls greallocn which calls grealloc; when entries is nullptr, grealloc acts as malloc returning uninitialized memory. The XRefEntry struct contains flags which is never zeroed by the allocator.

code: if (reserve(newSize) < newSize) return size; for (int i = size; i < newSize; ++i) { ... entries[i].flags = 0; ... }
note: resize only initializes entries from size to newSize-1. If constructXRef later accesses an entry with index < size that was never written by resize (because the entry was allocated in a prior reserve call but its flags field was never set), flags remains uninitialized.
getEntry calls readXRefUntil which may call constructXRef. After constructXRef returns, entries[i] may have type != xrefEntryNone but flags still uninitialized.
makeStream calls getEntry to obtain the XRefEntry for the stream object number. The returned entry pointer points to an entry whose flags field may be uninitialized.
setFlag reads entry->flags via 'flags |= mask', performing an uninitialized memory read when flags was never written. This is the MSAN 'UNKNOWN READ' crash site.

code: void setFlag(Flag flag, bool val) { if (val) flags |= flag; else flags &= ~flag; }
note: The inline setFlag reads the uninitialized flags field. Since flags was never assigned in constructXRef for this entry, the bitwise OR reads garbage, causing MSAN to report an uninitialized-value error.
